children: Provident Financial Services' net interest income and net income fell from the year-earlier quarter. Higher net interest income, driven by new loans at current market rates and favorable deposit repricing, and stronger noninterest income were offset by higher expenses, including a debt-extinguishment loss and core system conversion costs.
² Reported as “Net income”. ³ Reported as “Diluted earnings per share”.
: Rose $13.7 million to $208.0 million, primarily as new loans at current market rates and favorable deposit repricing lifted income.
: Increased 7 basis points to 3.50%; the average cost of interest-bearing liabilities fell 17 basis points to 2.79%.
: Increased $3.1 million to $30.5 million, driven by a $3.8 million increase in bank-owned life insurance income and higher insurance agency income.
: Provision for credit losses on loans was $7.2 million, primarily reflecting increased specific reserves and overall loan portfolio growth.
: Noninterest expense rose $27.6 million, including a $17.5 million debt-extinguishment loss and $3.7 million in core system conversion costs.
